subtopic: Magnetic Effect of Current — Conductor, Loop and Solenoid
stem:
The pattern of the magnetic field produced inside a current carrying solenoid is:

(The four options are figures: (A) curved, diverging field lines looping around the coil like the external field of a bar magnet; (B) straight, parallel field lines running uniformly through the inside of the solenoid with the lines looping round at the two ends; (C) concentric circles around a point; (D) straight parallel horizontal lines with arrows, shown without any return loops.)

options.label: A
options.text: Curved, diverging field lines looping around the coil (bar-magnet-like external pattern).

options.label: B
options.text: Straight, uniform, parallel field lines inside the solenoid, looping round at the ends (bar-magnet-like pattern).

options.label: C
options.text: Concentric circles around a central point.

options.label: D
options.text: Straight parallel horizontal lines with no return loops.

subtopic: Magnets, Magnetic Field and Field Lines
stem:
Figure shows the magnetic field lines between the two faces A and B of two magnets.

(In the figure two rectangular pole-faces A on the left and B on the right face each other. The field lines run continuously from face A across to face B, the arrowheads pointing from A towards B.)

options.label: A
options.text: One direction at any point in space

options.label: B
options.text: Both faces A and B of two bar magnets are North pole.

options.label: C
options.text: Face A is south pole while face B is north pole.

options.label: D
options.text: Both faces A and B of two bar magnets are South pole.

subtopic: Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor and Electric Motor
stem:
One end of a wire carrying current in the downward direction is placed in a trough containing mercury (so that the direction of force experienced by it is clearly visible). Two pole pieces N and S are placed on each side as shown in the diagram (so as to provide uniform magnetic field). What is the direction of force experienced by the wire?

(In the figure the wire hangs vertically with the current directed downward into the mercury; the N pole is on the left and the S pole is on the right, so the magnetic field points from left to right.)

subtopic: Magnetic Effect of Current — Conductor, Loop and Solenoid
stem:
Concentric circles with arrows centred at the wire AB are shown in figure.

(In the figure a straight vertical wire has end A at the top and end B at the bottom; the magnetic field around it is drawn as concentric circles whose arrows point anti-clockwise as seen looking along the wire.)

options.label: A
options.text: Current flows from A to B

options.label: B
options.text: Current flows from B to A

subtopic: Magnetic Effect of Current — Conductor, Loop and Solenoid
stem:
The correct pattern of magnetic field lines of the field produced by a current carrying circular loop is:

(The four options are figures of a vertical circular loop with face N on the left and face S on the right: (A) field lines forming two separate closed loops above and below the wire, not joined through the centre; (B) symmetric concentric circles around the top and bottom of the wire that merge into an elliptical dipole envelope, with straight lines through the centre of the loop; (C) the same envelope but with a concentric circle only at the bottom of the wire; (D) an elliptical envelope with nearly straight parallel lines through the centre and few concentric circles near the wire.)

options.label: A
options.text: Field lines forming two separate closed loops above and below the wire.

options.label: B
options.text: Symmetric concentric circles at top and bottom merging into a dipole envelope, straight through the centre.

options.label: C
options.text: Dipole envelope with a concentric circle only at the bottom of the wire.

options.label: D
options.text: Elliptical envelope with nearly straight parallel lines through the centre.

subtopic: Magnetic Effect of Current — Conductor, Loop and Solenoid
stem:
The magnetic field lines produced by a long straight current-carrying conductor are drawn over the horizontal plane ABCD, with the conductor passing perpendicularly through the plane at point O. The lines are:

(In the figure a long straight conductor in a circuit with a variable resistance, a cell and a key passes vertically through the centre O of a horizontal plane ABCD.)

options.label: A
options.text: concentric circles near the point O but of elliptical shapes as we go away from it

options.label: B
options.text: straight lines parallel to each other

subtopic: Magnetic Effect of Current — Conductor, Loop and Solenoid
stem:
A circular loop placed in a plane perpendicular to the plane of paper carries a current when the key is ON. The current as seen from points A and B (in the plane of the paper and on the axis of the coil) is anti-clockwise and clockwise respectively. The magnetic field lines point from B to A. The N-pole of the resultant magnet is on the face close to:

(In the figure a vertical circular loop has face A on the left and face B on the right; it is connected to a cell, a variable resistance and a key K.)

options.label: B
options.text: B if the current is small and A if the current is large

options.label: D
options.text: A if the current is small, and B if the current is large

subtopic: Magnetic Effect of Current — Conductor, Loop and Solenoid
stem:
The resultant magnetic field at point P situated midway between two parallel wires (placed horizontally, each carrying a steady current \(I\)) is:

(In the figure the upper wire AB carries current from A to B and the lower wire CD carries current from C to D, both currents flowing to the right; the point P lies midway between the two wires.)

options.label: A
options.text: in the same direction as the current in the wires.
